elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Revised 13.2: "Ono may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time, for any reasons..." The delayed commencement tied to the later of two redacted periods after First Commercial Sale is deleted, so the right exists from the Effective Date. This agreement has no Order Form structure, so the Agreement-level right is the full scope required.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Array" replaces the redacted [ * ] notice period; the retained rationale-with-notice condition is an existing, non-blocking formality rather than an added trigger.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "in which case Array shall refund on a pro rata basis any prepaid fees or other amounts prepaid by Ono for the period after the effective date of such termination" — pro rata is express, not merely inferred from a post-termination period, and the Section 6.1 non-refundability sentence is expressly subordinated ("Except as provided in Section 13.2") so no retained sentence contradicts the refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The only without-cause exit in Article 13 is 13.2, which runs to Ono alone (heading "Termination by Ono without Cause"); Array's remaining exits are for cause (13.3 material breach, 13.4 bankruptcy) and the 13.5 Safety/Efficacy right runs to Ono. Nothing in the rendered language creates or preserves an Array convenience right during the term running to expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term under 13.1.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Notice is fixed at thirty (30) days, which is outside the literal 60–90 day fallback band (and better for us); the fallback level is therefore not literally satisfied, but the preferred level is.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: revised 13.2 imposes no early-termination fee, penalty, instalment or contingent payment on Ono for exercising the convenience right, so no cap is needed.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Array has no convenience termination right at all under Article 13, which is stronger than a term-end-only restriction.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: there is no Array convenience termination right to which a notice period could attach.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met in operative language (30-day at-will right, express pro rata refund, no Array convenience exit).

The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" returned false, but inspected in substance this is a regex artefact — the rendered 13.2 reads "Ono may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time... upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice", using the party alias (Ono) rather than the generic 'Customer', so the element is in fact present.

Minimality holds: only the delayed First-Commercial-Sale commencement was removed, the notice period fixed and the refund sentence added; the heading, the "for any reasons" language and the rationale-with-notice condition are retained, and the model-language surplus "in whole or in part" was correctly omitted (no Order Form or partial-termination structure here).

Operation 2 is a narrow "Except as provided in Section 13.2" carve-out rather than a broad notwithstanding override, and it is necessary to prevent the retained Section 6.1 non-refundability sentence from contradicting the new refund obligation.

Watch point (not a failure): the refund reaches "prepaid fees or other amounts prepaid by Ono", which is broader than the checklist's "prepaid fees". It is Customer-favourable and stays within the refund element, but if Array pushes back, narrowing to "prepaid fees" and dropping the 6.1 carve-out (the ¥3.5bn upfront licence fee is arguably not a fee "for the period after" termination) would be the cleaner minimal landing.

Intent preserved: 13.1's term, expiry and post-expiry licence mechanics, and the 13.3–13.5 for-cause and safety/efficacy exits, are untouched; no dangling cross-reference or undefined term is created (Section 13.2 is a live reference).
